# Test File Output Template

The `/from-issue` skill renders generated test files following this template. The top-of-file comment block is **mandatory** and identical across every freshly-generated file (only the date, ticket key, source URL, and title vary; augmented files additionally gain an `Augmented by:` line — see Rules).

## Template

```typescript
// Generated by /from-issue on YYYY-MM-DD from Jira <KEY>.
// Source: <jira-issue-url>
// Title: <summary>
// Manual edits are welcome — this file is not regenerated automatically.
// Re-running /from-issue against a contributing issue will refuse to overwrite.

**Provenance when the run used `--from-file`** (workflow Step 2): line 1 reads
`from local file <path>` instead of `from Jira <KEY>`, and the `// Source:` line is that same
path — never a Jira URL. A spec must never claim a ticket that was never read.
The `// Title:` line still carries the summary from the file's front matter.

import LoginPage from '@pages/LoginPage';
import CatalogPage from '@pages/CatalogPage';
import { itFails } from '@utils/expected-failure'; // only when a test is locked to a defect

// One describe per feature, titled '<feature> — <context-label>'. Every test starts from a
// fresh app process, logged out (see "Session" below), so the context label is `no auth`.
describe('<feature> — no auth', () => {
  describe('Positive', () => {
    it('<behavior description>', async () => {
      // Specs do not call step(). Named steps come from the Page Object's action methods.
      await LoginPage.open();
      await LoginPage.loginAs('<username>', '<password>');
      await expect(CatalogPage.title).toHaveText('<expected>');
    });

    it('<behavior description> @smoke', async () => {
      // A smoke test carries @smoke at the END of its title — see Rules.
    });
  });

  describe('Negative', () => {
    it('<behavior description>', async () => {
      // ... one it(...) per Negative record
    });

    // <DEFECT-KEY> — <one line: what the application does that it should not>.
    // Replace itFails with it when <DEFECT-KEY> is fixed; this test turning red is the notification.
    itFails('<DEFECT-KEY>', '<behavior description>', async () => {
      // ... asserts the INTENDED behaviour, exactly as the AC states it
    });
  });

  describe('Edge', () => {
    it('<behavior description>', async () => {
      // ... one it(...) per Edge record
    });
  });
  // Omit any bucket describe whose record list is empty.
});
```

## Rules

- **Comment block at top** — mandatory. On first generation it is 5 lines with `YYYY-MM-DD`, `<KEY>`, `<jira-issue-url>`, and `<summary>` substituted:

  ```ts
  // Generated by /from-issue on YYYY-MM-DD from Jira <KEY>.
  // Source: <jira-issue-url>
  // Title: <summary>
  // Manual edits are welcome — this file is not regenerated automatically.
  // Re-running /from-issue against a contributing issue will refuse to overwrite.
  ```

  When the file is **augmented** by a later ticket (per ADR-0010), a `// Augmented by:` line is inserted directly below `// Title:`, listing each augmenting ticket as `<KEY> (YYYY-MM-DD)`, comma-separated:

  ```ts
  // Title: <summary>
  // Augmented by: OR-4 (2026-05-26), OR-7 (2026-06-02)
  ```

  **A file written by hand has no provenance block.** Augmenting one: put the `// Augmented by:` line on line 1, followed by the last two lines of the block (`Manual edits are welcome…`, `Re-running /from-issue…`). Do not invent a `Generated by` line — the file was not generated.

  The **contributor set** the skill uses for idempotency (Step 8) = the origin `<KEY>` on line 1 (if any) ∪ every key on the `Augmented by:` line.

- **Imports**:
  - Each Page Object the spec uses, as its default export: `import LoginPage from '@pages/LoginPage'`. Page Objects are singletons; there are no fixtures and nothing is constructed in the spec.
  - `describe`, `it` and `expect` are globals (Mocha + `expect-webdriverio`). Do not import them.
  - `import { itFails } from '@utils/expected-failure'` only when a test is locked to a defect.

- **Describe wrap — one describe per feature**: `describe('<feature> — no auth', () => { ... })`. The label is `no auth` because every test starts logged out; a test that needs a session logs in as its first action, and its title says who (`bod@example.com logs in and …`).

- **Bucket structure** — inside the feature describe, group tests into up to three nested `describe('Positive' | 'Negative' | 'Edge', () => { ... })` blocks. Order is fixed: **Positive → Negative → Edge**. Omit a bucket describe with zero tests. Classification rules: [`bucket-classification.md`](bucket-classification.md).

- **Per-test title — behaviour prose, then tags at the END.** Mocha has no tag option: `npm run test:smoke` selects tests with `--mochaOpts.grep @smoke`, which matches the **title**. So a smoke test's title ends in ` @smoke`:
  - smoke: `it('alice@example.com is rejected as locked out @smoke', async () => { ... })`
  - not smoke: `it('an empty password is rejected with "Enter Password"', async () => { ... })`

  Keep tags at the end, after the prose, so the title still reads as a sentence and a grep for the prose still finds it. `@smoke` is the only tag; there are no routing tags (no per-user projects exist to route to).

- **Expected failures — `itFails`, never `it.skip`.** A test for an AC the application contradicts, **after a person has confirmed the defect and filed it** (ADR-0024), is written with `itFails('<DEFECT-KEY>', '<title>', fn)`. It runs for real, passes while the defect lives, and fails the day it is fixed. The key is a required argument; the comment above the call names the defect and says how to remove the marker. The helper appends `[expected failure: <KEY>]` to the title so the report shows it. **Never apply it on your own initiative** — see `fix-loop.md`.

- **No raw locators in tests** — per ADR-0001 rule #4. Tests call Page methods and assert on the locators a Page exposes; they never build a `$()` themselves.
- **No `browser.pause()`, no fixed sleeps** — lint fails `browser.pause()`. Use auto-waiting assertions (`await expect(el).toHaveText(...)`), and for an absence, a bounded Page Object query (see [`wdio-conventions.md`](wdio-conventions.md) "Asserting that something does NOT happen").
- **Selector preference order** is the Page Object's concern, not the test's.

## Session

There is no `storageState`. A Mocha root hook terminates and relaunches the app before every test, so each test starts on the launch screen, logged out, with nothing in memory (ADR-0040). A test that needs a session logs in through `LoginPage` as its first action. If the AC text doesn't name a user, use the account the ticket or the login screen documents for the happy path, and record the choice as an assumption.

## Example: an augmented file

```typescript
// Augmented by: OR-1 (2026-09-21)
// Manual edits are welcome — this file is not regenerated automatically.
// Re-running /from-issue against a contributing issue will refuse to overwrite.

import LoginPage from '@pages/LoginPage';
import CatalogPage from '@pages/CatalogPage';
import { itFails } from '@utils/expected-failure';

const NAVIGATION_WINDOW_MS = 5_000; // measured: a sign-in reaches the catalog ~1.2 s after the tap

describe('Login — no auth', () => {
  describe('Negative', () => {
    it('alice@example.com is rejected as locked out @smoke', async () => {
      await LoginPage.open();
      await LoginPage.loginAs('alice@example.com', '10203040');
      await expect(LoginPage.passwordError).toHaveText('Sorry this user has been locked out.');
    });

    // OR-4 — the app signs in with any credential. Replace itFails with it when
    // OR-4 is fixed; this test turning red is the notification.
    itFails('OR-4', 'a wrong password does not open the catalog', async () => {
      await LoginPage.open();
      await LoginPage.loginAs('bod@example.com', 'xxxxxxxx');
      expect(await CatalogPage.opensWithin(NAVIGATION_WINDOW_MS)).toBe(false);
    });
  });
});
```

The run record's named steps come from the Page Object's action methods (each wraps its body in one `step`), not from the spec.
